location: No breaking step found. Checked in full: (2), (3), (5)–(16) and the final combination.
objection:
I found no error or gap. The proof is a self-contained elementary argument with truncation H = ⌊x^{2/5}⌋. It gives |C_x(m) − (x−m)𝔖(m)| ≤ (67+2D)x^{4/5} with an absolute constant, which is stronger than the stated bound. Each step checked:
(2) The divisor bound τ(n) ≤ D n^{1/10} is correct. For p ≥ 2^{10}, a+1 ≤ 2^a ≤ p^{a/10}. For p < 2^{10}, (a+1)p^{-a/10} ≤ Σ(j+1)p^{-j/10} = (1−p^{-1/10})^{-2}.
(3) All four sum bounds are correct. The real-t tail uses j>t ⇔ j>⌊t⌋ and ⌊t⌋ ≥ t/2 for t ≥ 1.
(5)–(7) |T_H(k)| ≤ τ(k) holds. Both I_0 and I_m are subsets of {1,…,⌊x⌋}, because m+L = x. So the number of multiples of d² in either set is ≤ ⌊x/d²⌋, and Σ_{d>H} x/d² ≤ x/H.
(8) The product identity μ²μ² − TT = R(n)μ²(n+m) + T(n)R(n+m) is exact. With n ≤ L ≤ x and H ≥ x^{2/5}/2 (valid for x ≥ 2, since then H ≥ 1), it gives 2x^{3/5} + 2Dx^{7/10}.
(9)–(10) The CRT solvability condition (d,e)²|m is correct, and the modulus is d²e²/(d,e)². The count ⌊(L−r)/h⌋ − ⌊−r/h⌋ = L/h + θ with |θ| < 1 is correct for real L ≥ 0. There are at most H² pairs, so the error is ≤ x^{4/5}.
(11)–(13) The change of variables d = ga, e = gb gives an upper bound after the coprimality condition is dropped. For g ≤ H the tail term is 4/(gH); for g > H it is 4/g². Together this gives (8 + 4 log H)/H, doubled by symmetry. The bound does not depend on m.
(14) The Euler product is justified by absolute convergence and exhaustion over finite sets of primes. The local factors 1 − 2/p² + 1_{p²|m}/p² are correct and give exactly 𝔖(m) as defined in the statement.
(15)–(16) log x ≤ 5x^{1/5} holds, and the constants add up correctly.
Uniformity: when x−m is bounded or zero, both sides are handled, since all bounds hold for every real L ≥ 0. Statement ranges: real x ≥ 2 and integer 1 ≤ m ≤ x, both matched. The proof cites no external results and uses no dependencies, so checklist items 4, 5 and 8 do not apply. All interchanges of summation are over finite sums or absolutely convergent series. The circle-method cutoff in the statement is only permitted, not required, so not using it is fine.
Numerical sanity checks agree with the proof:
- For x = 2·10^5 and several m, the error |C_x(m) − (x−m)𝔖(m)| is at most about 22, far below x^{4/5} ≈ 17411.
- |A_H(m) − 𝔖(m)| is well below 8(2 + log H)/H for H ∈ {5, 20, 60, 200} and several m.
other_issues: Cosmetic: in the text before (7), the remark that the outer sum has at most √x terms is never used; the bound only needs Σ_{d>H} 1/d² ≤ 1/H.
Cosmetic: the absolute constant D = ∏_{p<2^{10}}(1−p^{-1/10})^{-2} is astronomically large. That is harmless because the statement only asks for some C(ε).
